newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico upholds ammonium sulfate U.S. import tariff.
newsitem.headline: Mexico upholds ammonium sulfate U.S. import tariff.

text.p: Mexico decided to uphold its tariff on ammonium sulfate imports from the United States, the Trade Ministry (Secofi) said Monday in Official Gazette.
Secofi said the tariff will be applied only when the price per tonne is less than an average of $97.18 and that the tariff cannot exceed 57.91 percent.
"Prices less than an average of $97.18 per tonne will pay a compensatory tariff that is the difference between the ammonium sulfate export price and the normal average price," Secofi said.

U.S. companies such as BASF Corp, DBA Chemical Enterprises, DSM Chemicals North America Inc. and Zipp Industries, which did not export ammonium sulfate during the past 18 months of investigations, can request a special tariff, the Secofi added.
In 1995, Mexico imported about 18,000 tonnes of ammonium sulfate, it said.
Charges of unfair ammonium sulfate import pricing from the U.S. surfaced about two years ago from local producers.
